title: The Daily-Wage Labourer With a Growing Neck Swelling

sections.heading: The Patient's Story
sections.content:
She is 35 years old, works as a daily-wage labourer, and came in because of swelling on the left side of her neck. She had been completely well until three years ago, when she suddenly noticed a swelling about 3x3 cm on that side of her neck. Since then, two more swellings, each about 1x2 cm, have appeared and have been slowly growing over the last two years. All of them feel firm.

Alongside this, over the past 15 days, she has had a dragging type of headache with blurring of vision, nausea, and vomiting — worse around midday — and her sleep has been disturbed. She has not noticed any swelling in her armpits or groin, and denies fever, cough, weight loss, mouth ulcers, vaginal discharge, or painful intercourse.

Her past history includes kidney stones four years ago and a slipped disc, also four years ago. Further back, 18 years ago, she had joint pains for which she used an herbal medication three times a day for about a year; the joint pains recurred for two more years before eventually settling.

Her periods started at age 13, and her cycles run 3 days out of every 28, without clots or painful periods.

sections.heading: What the Work-Up Showed So Far
sections.content:
- **General appearance:** no pallor, icterus, clubbing, or cyanosis
- **Vitals:** BP 110/70 mmHg, pulse 88 bpm, RR 22/min
- **Local examination of the neck swelling:** a 3x3 cm swelling along with two smaller lymph nodes each about 0.5x0.5 cm; soft in consistency, mobile, discrete, and non-tender, without local warmth, overlying skin changes, or matting
- **Other lymph node groups:** normal, with no axillary or inguinal lymphadenopathy
- **Cardiovascular exam:** normal heart sounds, no murmurs
- **Respiratory exam:** bilateral air entry equal
- **Abdominal exam:** soft, non-tender
- **Neurological exam:** no abnormality detected
